cap: The three common causes of vaginal discharge separate on two bedside tests. The pH splits them first: bacterial vaginosis and trichomoniasis push it above 4.5, while candidiasis leaves it normal. The slide then names the cause: clue cells, motile trichomonads, or pseudohyphae on a KOH prep.
teach: Read the grid down a column to build the picture of one infection, and across a row to find the single feature that separates them. The pH row and the microscopy row do most of the work; odor, discharge and the strawberry cervix support the answer. The treatment row explains the classic trap: metronidazole covers both high-pH causes, but only trichomoniasis requires partner treatment, and an antibiotic makes Candida worse.
